text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crown Prince Hassan tells the World Affairs Council Jordan can be a leading example for thought and learning. "We see Iraq as a brother and supporter and we back Palestinian self-determination and statehood.
- New confrontations possible between Iraq and U.S. as Barzani's forces take two towns on the road to Sulaimaniya.
- Two U.S. companies to start digging for oil soon in Dead Sea region.
- Prime Minister Kabariti meets Parliamentary speaker Srour to discuss forthcoming parliamentary session.
- Crown Prince Hassan says there's no going back on reforms. "The transition stage will be tough, but we will get through it by national dialogue."
- Supply Minister Sobar tours shops in the capital to check they are selling goods at right prices after some traders raised prices unjustifiably.
- U.S. Under-Secretary of State for Economic and Business Affairs Joan Spero says signing of $200 million trade guarantee with Jordan on Saturday is important step in deepening economic ties.
- Head of Civil Service Commission Olayan says unemployment is lower than officially announced 15 percent of workforce.
- Crown Prince Hassan affirms importance of opening Jordan up to the world. Confirms economic performance is competitive and politics based on participation.
- Israeli tourism minister Katzav arriving in Jordan today for talks on Dead Sea tourism.
